Private notes app

Rapier Notes keeps your notes on your device, as plain Markdown files shown as cards. Pin and color them, add checklists, pictures and voice notes, and go back to any earlier version. Import brings in Google Keep, Apple Notes, Evernote, Notion, Obsidian and more. There is no account. The Android app adds reminders and a home-screen widget.

Also: Free online Markdown editor · Free drawing app online

Questions

Is it a Google Keep alternative?

Yes. Import your Google Keep notes from a Google Takeout export: text, checklists, pins and pictures become Markdown notes.

Where are my notes kept?

On your device, in your browser or the Android app. Nothing is uploaded unless you turn on sync to storage you own.

Is there an Android app?

Yes, Rapier on Google Play. It has no internet permission.

Is it free?

Yes. Rapier is free and open source, with no account, ads or tracking.

Open Notes from the ••• menu at the top right.

Every note is a Markdown file shown as a card. Pin, color, sort into sections, attach pictures and voice notes. You can turn on proper checklists inside Notes and, if you use the Android app, add reminders and other native features. Search your notes, link and tag them, and restore any earlier version. Import brings in Google Keep, Apple Notes, Evernote, Notion, Obsidian and more. Backup saves everything as one ZIP file. Sync keeps them in your own Cloudflare account, encrypted with a key that never leaves your device.

Tip. Back up the notes you care about. The Android app keeps notes in its own files, outside Android's automatic backup.
